verses.text: Paul, called by God's will to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and our brother Sosthenes,
to God's church in Corinth—to those made holy in Christ Jesus and called to be his holy people, along with everyone everywhere who calls on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God for the grace he gave you in Christ Jesus.
In him you have been enriched in every way—with all kinds of speech and knowledge—
just as the message about Christ was firmly established among you.
So you aren't missing any spiritual gift as you wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed.
He will keep you strong to the end, so you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful. He called you into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
Brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, I urge you all to agree with one another. Don't let there be divisions among you; be united in your thinking and purpose.
People from Chloe's household have told me, my brothers and sisters, that there are arguments among you.
Here's what I mean: each of you says, ‘I follow Paul,’ ‘I follow Apollos,’ ‘I follow Cephas,’ or ‘I follow Christ.’
Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized in Paul's name?
I'm thankful I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so no one can say you were baptized in my name.
(I also baptized Stephanas's household. Beyond that, I don't remember baptizing anyone else.)
Christ didn't send me to baptize, but to announce the Good News—and not with clever speech, so that Christ's cross wouldn't lose its power.
The message of the cross sounds foolish to those headed for destruction, but to us who are being saved, it's God's power.
As Scripture says, ‘I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and bring the cleverness of the clever to nothing.’
Where are the wise? Where are the experts in the law? Where are the debaters of this age? Hasn't God shown the world's wisdom to be foolish?
Since the world couldn't know God through its own wisdom, God was pleased to save those who believe through what the world calls the foolish message we preach.
Jews ask for signs, and Greeks look for wisdom,
but we preach Christ crucified—a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles.
But to those God has called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is God's power and God's wisdom.
For God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength.
Brothers and sisters, look at who God called: not many of you were wise by human standards, powerful, or high-born.
But God chose what the world calls foolish to shame the wise, and what the world calls weak to shame the strong.
God chose what the world considers low and despised—even what seems to be nothing—to bring to nothing what the world considers important,
so that no one can brag in God's presence.
Because of God, you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God—our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
So, as Scripture says, ‘If you brag, brag about the Lord.’
When I came to you, brothers and sisters, I didn't come with impressive words or human wisdom as I announced God's truth.
I had decided to focus on nothing among you except Jesus Christ—and him crucified.
I came to you feeling weak, afraid, and deeply shaken.
My words and my preaching weren't clever or persuasive. They showed the Spirit's power,
so your faith wouldn't rest on human wisdom but on God's power.
We do speak wisdom among the mature, but it's not the wisdom of this age or its rulers, who are fading away.
We speak God's wisdom, a mystery once hidden, which God planned before the ages for our glory.
None of this age's rulers understood it. If they had, they wouldn't have crucified the Lord of glory.
But, as Scripture says, ‘What no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined—this is what God has prepared for those who love him.’
God has revealed these things to us through the Spirit. The Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
Who knows a person's thoughts except that person's own spirit within them? In the same way, no one knows God's thoughts except God's Spirit.
We didn't receive the spirit of the world. We received the Spirit who comes from God, so we can understand the gifts God has freely given us.
We speak about these things, not with words taught by human wisdom, but with words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual truths to spiritual people.
A person without the Spirit doesn't welcome the things that come from God's Spirit. They seem foolish, and that person can't understand them because they're spiritually discerned.
But the person who has the Spirit can discern all things, though no one can judge them.
As Scripture says, ‘Who has known the Lord's mind well enough to instruct him?’ But we have the mind of Christ.
Brothers and sisters, I couldn't talk to you as Spirit-led people, but as people shaped by human nature—as infants in Christ.
I fed you milk, not solid food, because you weren't ready for it. And you're still not ready,
because you're still living by human nature. As long as jealousy, arguments, and divisions are among you, aren't you living by human nature and acting like everyone else?
When one of you says, ‘I follow Paul,’ and another, ‘I follow Apollos,’ aren't you acting like everyone else?
So who is Apollos? Who is Paul? We're servants through whom you came to believe, each doing what the Lord assigned.
I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.
So the one who plants and the one who waters aren't the main thing. God, who makes it grow, is.
The one who plants and the one who waters share the same purpose, and each will be rewarded according to their own work.
We are God's co-workers. You are God's field, God's building.
By God's grace to me, I laid a foundation like a skilled builder, and someone else is building on it. Each person must be careful how they build.
No one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid: Jesus Christ.
Some may build on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw.
Each person's work will become clear. The Day will reveal it, because it will be uncovered by fire; the fire will test the quality of each person's work.
If what someone built on the foundation survives, they'll receive a reward.
If their work burns up, they'll suffer loss. They themselves will be saved, but only as someone escaping through fire.
Don't you know that you are God's temple and God's Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy them. God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.
Don't fool yourselves. If any of you thinks you're wise by this world's standards, you should become a fool in this world's eyes so you can become truly wise.
The wisdom of this world is foolishness to God. Scripture says, ‘He catches the wise in their own cleverness.’
And again, ‘The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are pointless.’
So don't brag about people. Everything belongs to you:
whether Paul, Apollos, or Cephas; the world, life or death; the present or the future. Everything belongs to you,
you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
So, think of us as Christ's servants and stewards entrusted with God's mysteries.
What matters for a steward is to prove faithful.
It means very little to me if you judge me—or if any human court does. I don't even judge myself.
My conscience is clear, but that doesn't prove I'm in the right. The Lord is the one who judges me.

So don't judge anything before the right time. Wait until the Lord comes. He'll bring hidden things out into the light and reveal what's in people's hearts. Then each person will receive praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I've applied these examples to myself and Apollos for your sake, so you can learn not to go beyond what is written. Then none of you will get arrogant and take sides against one another.
Who made you different from anyone else? What do you have that you didn't receive? And if you received it, why brag as if it were your own achievement?
You already have everything you want! You're already rich! You've started ruling without us. I wish you really were ruling, so we could reign with you!
As I see it, God has put us apostles on display at the end of the procession, like people sentenced to die. We've become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels and to humans.
We're fools for Christ, but you think you're wise in Christ. We're weak, but you are strong. You get honor, while we get disrespect.
Even now we're hungry and thirsty, poorly clothed, beaten, and without a home.
We work hard with our own hands. When people insult us, we bless them; when we're persecuted, we endure.
When people slander us, we answer gently. We've become like the world's trash, the dirt everyone scrapes off—right up to now.
I'm not writing this to embarrass you. I'm warning you as my dearly loved children.
You may have ten thousand guardians in Christ, but you don't have many fathers. In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.
So I urge you: imitate me.
That's why I sent Timothy to you. He's my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, and he'll remind you how I live in Christ Jesus, just as I teach in every church everywhere.
Some of you have become arrogant, thinking I won't come to you.
But I'll come soon, if the Lord wills, and then I'll find out not just what these arrogant people say, but what power they have.
God's Kingdom isn't just talk; it's power.
What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or with love and a gentle spirit?
It's actually been reported that there's sexual immorality among you—so serious that even people outside the church don't do this: one man is living with his father's wife.
And you're proud? You should be grieving instead, so the person who did this would be removed from your community.
Though I'm away from you physically, I'm with you in spirit. I've already judged the person who did this, as if I were there.
When you gather in the name of our Lord Jesus, and my spirit is with you, act with the power of our Lord Jesus:
hand this person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that their spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your bragging isn't good. Don't you know a little yeast spreads through the whole batch of dough?
Clear out the old yeast so you can be a fresh batch, as you really are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
So let's celebrate—not with the old yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
I didn't mean the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy, swindlers, or idol worshipers. You'd have to leave the world to avoid them all.

What I meant was: don't associate with anyone who claims to be a brother or sister but is sexually immoral, greedy, an idol worshiper, an abusive slanderer, a drunkard, or a swindler. Don't even share a meal with such a person.
Why should I judge people outside the church? Aren't you supposed to judge those inside?
God will judge those outside. As Scripture says, ‘Remove the evil person from among you.’
How can any of you take a dispute with a neighbor to court before unjust judges instead of bringing it before God's people?
Don't you know that God's people will judge the world? If the world is to be judged by you, are you really unqualified to handle small disputes?
Don't you know we'll judge angels? How much more can we handle everyday matters?
So when you have disputes about everyday things, why appoint as judges people the church doesn't respect?
I'm saying this to make you feel ashamed. Is there really no one wise among you who can settle a dispute between fellow believers?
Instead, one believer takes another to court—and in front of unbelievers at that!
The fact that you have lawsuits against one another is already a failure. Why not accept being wronged? Why not let yourself be cheated?
But instead, you do wrong and cheat—and you do it to your own brothers and sisters.
Don't you know that people who do wrong won't inherit God's Kingdom? Don't be deceived: the sexually immoral, idol worshipers, adulterers, men who sell sex, men who have sex with men,
thieves, the greedy, drunkards, slanderers, and swindlers won't inherit God's Kingdom.
Some of you used to be like that. But you were washed clean, made holy, and made right in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
You say, ‘I'm allowed to do anything’—but not everything is helpful. ‘I'm allowed to do anything’—but I won't let anything control me.
You say, ‘Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food,’ but God will put an end to both. The body isn't meant for sexual immorality; it's meant for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
God raised the Lord from the dead, and by his power he will raise us too.
Don't you know your bodies are parts of Christ? Should I take parts of Christ and join them to a prostitute? Absolutely not!
Don't you know that the one who joins with a prostitute becomes one body with her? Scripture says, ‘The two will become one flesh.’
But the one who joins with the Lord is one spirit with him.
Run from sexual immorality! Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against their own body.
Don't you know your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who lives in you and was given to you by God? You don't belong to yourself.
You were bought at a price. So honor God with your body and your spirit, which belong to him.
Now, about the questions you sent me: it can be good for a man to refrain from sexual relations with a woman.
But because sexual immorality is a real danger, each husband should have his own wife, and each wife her own husband.
A husband should give his wife the affection he owes her, and a wife should do the same for her husband.
A wife’s body isn’t hers alone; her husband shares that authority. In the same way, a husband’s body isn’t his alone; his wife shares that authority.
Don’t withhold from each other—unless you both agree to pause for a short time so you can focus on prayer and fasting. Then come back together, so Satan won’t tempt you when self-control is hard.
I’m saying this as a concession, not laying down a command.
I wish everyone could live as I do, but each person has their own gift from God—one kind for this person, another kind for someone else.
So here’s what I say to unmarried people and widows: it can be good to stay single like me.
But if self-control is a struggle, marry. It’s better to marry than to keep burning with desire.
To people who are married, this is the Lord’s command, not just my take: a wife should not leave her husband.
(But if she does leave, she should stay unmarried or reconcile with her husband.) And a husband should not divorce his wife.
To everyone else, this is my instruction, not a direct command from the Lord: if a believer has an unbelieving wife who’s willing to stay with him, he shouldn’t leave her.
And if a believing woman has an unbelieving husband who’s willing to stay with her, she shouldn’t leave him.
The unbelieving husband is made holy in relation to his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife in relation to her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
But if the unbelieving spouse chooses to leave, let them go. The believing brother or sister isn’t bound to force the relationship. God called us to live in peace.
Wife, how do you know you’ll save your husband? Husband, how do you know you’ll save your wife?
Still, each person should live in the situation the Lord assigned and the life God called them to. That’s my direction for every church.
Were you circumcised when God called you? Don’t undo it. Were you uncircumcised? Don’t get circumcised.
Circumcision isn’t the point, and uncircumcision isn’t either. What matters is keeping God’s commands.
Each person should stay in the situation they were in when God called them.
Were you enslaved when God called you? Don’t let that crush you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
The person called while enslaved is free in the Lord. And the person who was free when called is Christ’s servant.
You were bought at a price. Don’t become people’s slaves.
Family, in whatever situation God called you, stay there with God.
About unmarried women: I don’t have a command from the Lord, but I’ll give my judgment as someone the Lord showed mercy to and made trustworthy.
With the hard times we’re facing, I think it’s good for a person to stay as they are.
Are you married? Don’t try to get out of it. Are you unmarried? Don’t go looking for a wife.
But if you marry, you haven’t sinned. If an unmarried woman marries, she hasn’t sinned either. Still, marriage can bring hardship in this life, and I want to spare you some of that.
Here’s what I mean, family: time is short. From now on, even people who have wives should live as though that isn’t their whole world;
those who grieve as though grief doesn’t own them; those who celebrate as though celebration isn’t everything; those who buy as though possessions aren’t theirs to keep;
and those who use the world should not get wrapped up in it. This world, as we know it, is passing away.
I want you free from unnecessary worries. An unmarried man can focus on the Lord’s concerns and how to please him;
but a married man also has worldly concerns—how to please his wife.

There’s a difference between a married woman and an unmarried woman. The unmarried woman can focus on the Lord’s concerns, being holy in body and spirit. The married woman has worldly concerns—how to please her husband.
I’m saying this for your good, not to trap you. I want you to live honorably and stay focused on the Lord without distractions.
If a man thinks he isn’t acting honorably toward the woman he’s pledged to, and the situation calls for marriage, he should do what he thinks right. He doesn’t sin; they should marry.
But if he’s settled in his heart, feels no pressure, and can manage his own decision, and has decided to keep her unmarried, he does well.
So the man who marries the woman he’s pledged to does well, and the one who doesn’t marry her does better.
A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. If he dies, she’s free to marry whoever she wants—but only in the Lord.
Still, I think she’ll be happier if she stays as she is. That’s my judgment, and I believe I have God’s Spirit too.
Now about food offered to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge can make people arrogant, but love builds people up.
If someone thinks they know something, they still don't know it the way they should.
But whoever loves God is known by God.
So about eating food offered to idols: we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God but one.
People may call many things ‘gods’ in heaven or on earth—there are many so-called gods and lords—
but for us there is one God, the Father, from whom everything comes and for whom we live; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom everything exists and through whom we live.
But not everyone has this understanding. Some are still so used to idols that when they eat food offered to an idol, they think of it as idol worship, and their weak conscience is stained.
Food doesn't bring us closer to God. We aren't worse off if we don't eat, or better off if we do.
But be careful that your freedom doesn't become a reason for someone with a weaker conscience to fall.
If someone with a weak conscience sees you, who understand this, eating in an idol's temple, won't they be encouraged to eat food offered to idols too?
Then your knowledge destroys the weak believer, a brother or sister Christ died for.
When you sin against your brothers and sisters in this way and wound their weak conscience, you're sinning against Christ.
So if food causes my brother or sister to fall, I'll never eat meat again, so I won't cause them to fall.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven't I seen Jesus our Lord? Aren't you the result of my work in the Lord?
Even if others don't consider me an apostle, I certainly am to you. You are the proof of my apostleship in the Lord.
Here's my defense to those who question me:
Don't we have the right to food and drink?
Don't we have the right to travel with a believing wife, like the other apostles, the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who have to work for a living?
Which soldier serves at their own expense? Who plants a vineyard without eating its fruit? Who tends a flock without drinking its milk?
Am I saying this just from a human point of view? Doesn't the law say the same thing?
Moses' law says, ‘Don't muzzle an ox while it's threshing grain.’ Is God concerned only about oxen?
Isn't he speaking for our sake? It was written for us, because the one who plows should plow with hope, and the one who threshes should do so expecting a share of the harvest.
If we planted spiritual things among you, is it too much to receive material support from you?
If others have this right to your support, don't we have it even more? Still, we haven't used this right. We put up with everything so we won't create an obstacle to Christ's Good News.
Don't you know that those who serve in the temple eat food from the temple, and those who serve at the altar share in what is offered there?
In the same way, the Lord directed that those who announce the Good News should receive their living from it.
But I haven't used any of these rights. And I'm not writing to ask you to do this for me. I'd rather die than let anyone take away this reason I have to boast.
If I preach the Good News, I have nothing to brag about—I'm obligated to do it. How terrible it would be for me if I didn't preach it!
If I chose to do this on my own, I could expect a reward. But even if I don't choose it, I've still been entrusted with a responsibility.
So what is my reward? That when I preach the Good News, I can offer it free of charge and not make full use of my rights as a preacher.
Even though I'm free from everyone, I made myself everyone's servant so I could win as many as possible.
To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law, I became like one under the law—though I'm not under the law myself—so I could win those under it.
To those without the law, I became like one without the law—though I'm not outside God's law, but under Christ's law—so I could win those without the law.
To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I've become all things to all people so that by every possible means I might save some.
I do all this for the sake of the Good News, so I can share in its blessings.
Don't you know that in a race everyone runs, but only one gets the prize? Run in a way that wins it.
Everyone who competes in the games trains with discipline. They do it for a crown that won't last, but we do it for one that lasts forever.
So I don't run without a clear goal. I don't fight like someone swinging at the air.
I train my body and make it my servant, so that after preaching to others I won't be disqualified myself.
Brothers and sisters, I don't want you to miss this: our ancestors were all under the cloud, and they all passed through the sea.
They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink. They drank from the spiritual rock that went with them, and that rock was Christ.
But God wasn't pleased with most of them, and they were struck down in the wilderness.
These events happened as examples for us, so we wouldn't crave evil things as they did.
Don't worship idols as some of them did. Scripture says, ‘The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to celebrate.’
Let's not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did—23,000 died in one day.
Let's not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
And don't grumble, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as examples, and were written down to warn us, who are living in these final times.
So if you think you're standing firm, be careful that you don't fall.

No temptation has come your way except what people commonly face. God is faithful; he won't let you be tempted beyond what you can handle. Along with the temptation, he'll provide a way through it so you can endure it.
So then, my dear friends, run from idol worship.
I'm speaking to sensible people. Judge for yourselves what I'm saying.
The cup of blessing that we bless—isn't it sharing in Christ's blood? The bread we break—isn't it sharing in Christ's body?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body, since we all share in that one loaf.
Look at Israel according to human descent: don't those who eat the sacrifices share in the altar?
So what am I saying? That food offered to idols has some special meaning, or that an idol is anything?
No. What the Gentiles sacrifice, they offer to demons, not to God. I don't want you sharing in fellowship with demons.
You can't drink the Lord's cup and the cup of demons too. You can't share the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than he is?
You say, ‘I'm allowed to do anything’—but not everything is useful. ‘I'm allowed to do anything’—but not everything builds people up.
No one should look out only for their own good, but for the good of others too.
Eat anything sold in the market without raising questions of conscience,
because, as Scripture says, ‘The earth belongs to the Lord, along with everything in it.’
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat whatever is served without asking questions of conscience.
But if someone tells you, ‘This was offered to idols,’ don't eat it—for the sake of the person who told you and their conscience.
I'm talking about the other person's conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I eat with gratitude, why should I be criticized for food I thank God for?
So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do everything for God's glory.
Don't be a reason anyone stumbles—Jews, Greeks, or God's church.
That's also what I try to do: please everyone in every way, not looking for my own advantage but for the good of many, so they may be saved.
Follow my example, just as I follow Christ's.
I commend you, brothers and sisters, because you remember me in everything and hold firmly to the traditions I passed on to you.
But I want you to understand that Christ is the head of every man, man is the head of woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Any man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
But any woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head—it is the same as if her head were shaved.
If a woman won't cover her head, she might as well cut her hair short. But if it's shameful for her to have short hair or a shaved head, she should cover her head.
A man shouldn't cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.
Man didn't come from woman; woman came from man.
And man wasn't created for woman; woman was created for man.
That's why a woman should have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
Still, in the Lord, woman isn't independent of man, and man isn't independent of woman.
Just as woman came from man, man is also born through woman. And everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it appropriate for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Doesn't nature itself teach you that long hair is dishonorable for a man,
while long hair is a woman's glory? Her hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we have no such practice, and neither do God's churches.
In giving this next instruction, I can't praise you, because your gatherings are doing more harm than good.
First, I hear that when you gather as a church there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
Some divisions are bound to happen, so that it becomes clear who among you is genuine.
When you come together, what you're eating isn't really the Lord's Supper.
As you eat, each person goes ahead with their own meal. One goes hungry while another gets drunk.
Don't you have homes where you can eat and drink? Or do you despise God's church and shame those who have nothing? What should I say? Should I praise you? I can't praise you for this.
I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: on the night he was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread.
After giving thanks, he broke it and said, ‘This is my body, given for you. Do this to remember me.’
In the same way, after supper he took the cup and said, ‘This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this to remember me.’
Every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you announce the Lord's death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in an unworthy way is guilty of sinning against the Lord's body and blood.
Everyone should examine themselves, and then eat the bread and drink from the cup.
Anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on themselves.
That's why many of you are weak and sick, and some have died.
If we examined ourselves, we wouldn't be judged.
But when the Lord judges us, he disciplines us so that we won't be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you gather to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, they should eat at home, so your gathering won't bring judgment. I'll deal with the other matters when I come.
Now, brothers and sisters, about spiritual gifts: I don't want you to be uninformed.
You remember that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray to worship idols that can't speak, however you were influenced.
So I want you to know: no one speaking by God's Spirit says, ‘Jesus is cursed,’ and no one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit gives them.
There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord is served.
There are different kinds of work, but the same God empowers everyone in every way.
The Spirit's presence is given to each person for the good of all.
To one, the Spirit gives a message of wisdom; to another, a message of knowledge, by the same Spirit.
To another, faith by the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing by that one Spirit.
To another, miraculous powers; to another, prophecy; to another, the ability to discern spirits; to another, different kinds of languages; and to another, the interpretation of languages.
One and the same Spirit brings all of this about, giving each person gifts as he chooses.
Just as one body has many parts, and all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.
We were all baptized by one Spirit into one body—Jews or Greeks, enslaved or free—and we were all given the same Spirit to drink.
The body isn't made up of one part, but many.
If the foot says, ‘I'm not a hand, so I don't belong to the body,’ that doesn't make it any less part of the body.
And if the ear says, ‘I'm not an eye, so I don't belong to the body,’ that doesn't make it any less part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, how would it hear? If the whole body were an ear, how would it smell?
But God arranged every part in the body exactly as he wanted it.
If all the parts were the same, where would the body be?
As it is, there are many parts but one body.
The eye can't tell the hand, ‘I don't need you!’ And the head can't tell the feet, ‘I don't need you!’
On the contrary, the parts that seem weaker are necessary.
The parts we think less honorable we treat with greater honor, and the parts we consider less presentable get special care,
while the presentable parts don't need extra care. God put the body together and gave greater honor to the parts that lacked it,
so there would be no division in the body, but that all the parts would care equally for one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it. If one part is honored, every part celebrates with it.
You are Christ's body, and each of you is a part of it.

God has appointed people in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then those who do miracles, those with gifts of healing, those who help, those who lead, and those who speak different languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in different languages? Do all interpret?
Eagerly seek the greater gifts. And now I'll show you a way that's far better.
If I could speak every human and angelic language but didn't have love, I'd be nothing but a loud gong or a crashing cymbal.
If I had the gift of prophecy and understood every mystery and all knowledge, and if I had enough faith to move mountains, but didn't have love, I would be nothing.
If I gave away everything I own to feed the poor, and even handed over my body to be burned, but didn't have love, I would gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. It doesn't envy or brag, and it isn't arrogant.
It doesn't act rudely, insist on its own way, or get irritated. It doesn't keep a record of wrongs.
Love doesn't celebrate wrongdoing; it celebrates the truth.
It bears all things, trusts all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
Love never ends. Prophecies will pass away, languages will stop, and knowledge will pass away.
We know only part, and we prophesy only part.
But when completeness comes, what is partial will pass away.
When I was a child, I spoke, thought, and reasoned like a child. When I became an adult, I left childish ways behind.
For now we see only a dim reflection, but then we'll see face to face. Now I know only part, but then I'll know fully, just as God fully knows me.
For now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. And the greatest of these is love.
Pursue love, and eagerly desire spiritual gifts—especially the gift of prophecy.
The one who speaks in a language no one knows speaks to God, not to people. No one understands them; by the Spirit they speak mysteries.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people to strengthen, encourage, and comfort them.
Speaking in a language no one else understands strengthens the speaker, but prophecy strengthens the church.

I want you all to speak in other languages, but even more, I want you to prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in languages, unless someone interprets so the church can be built up.
Brothers and sisters, if I came to you speaking in languages you don't understand, how would that help you unless I also brought a revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?
Even lifeless instruments like a flute or harp have to make distinct notes. Otherwise, how would anyone recognize the tune?
And if a trumpet gives an unclear signal, who will get ready for battle?
It's the same with you: if you don't speak words people can understand, how will anyone know what you're saying? You'll just be talking into the air.
There may be many languages in the world, and not one of them is meaningless.
But if I don't know what someone's language means, we'll be strangers to each other.
Since you're eager for spiritual gifts, seek to excel in gifts that build up the church.
So the one who speaks in another language should pray for the ability to interpret it.
If I pray in a language I don't understand, my spirit is praying, but my mind isn't producing anything useful.
So what should I do? I'll pray with my spirit, and I'll pray with my mind too. I'll sing with my spirit, and I'll sing with my mind too.
Otherwise, if you give thanks in the spirit, how can someone who doesn't understand say ‘Amen’ to your thanksgiving? They don't know what you're saying.
You may be giving thanks well, but the other person isn't being built up.
I thank God that I speak in other languages more than all of you.
But in church I'd rather say five words that I understand, so I can teach others, than ten thousand words in a language no one understands.
Brothers and sisters, don't think like children. Be innocent about evil, but mature in your thinking.
The law says, ‘I will speak to this people through people who speak unfamiliar languages and through the lips of foreigners, but even then they won't listen to me, says the Lord.’
So languages are a sign for unbelievers, not believers; prophecy is a sign for believers, not unbelievers.
If the whole church gathers and everyone speaks in other languages, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, won't they say you're out of your minds?
But if everyone is prophesying and an unbeliever or outsider comes in, they'll be convicted by all and examined by all.
The secrets of their heart will be exposed. They'll fall facedown and worship God, saying, ‘God is truly among you!’
So, brothers and sisters, what should you do? When you gather, each person may have a song, a teaching, a revelation, a language, or an interpretation. Let everything be done to build people up.
If someone speaks in another language, let two—or at most three—speak, one at a time, and someone must interpret.
If there's no interpreter, the speaker should stay quiet in the church and speak privately to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said.
If someone sitting down receives a revelation, the first speaker should stop.
You can all prophesy one by one, so everyone can learn and be encouraged.
The spirits of prophets are under the control of the prophets.
God isn't a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of God's people.
Women should be quiet in the churches. They aren't permitted to speak, but should be in submission, as the law also says.
If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home. It's shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
Did God's word originate with you? Are you the only ones it has reached?
If anyone thinks they're a prophet or spiritual, they should recognize that what I'm writing is the Lord's command.
If anyone doesn't recognize this, they won't be recognized.
So, my brothers and sisters, eagerly desire to prophesy, and don't forbid speaking in other languages.
But let everything be done in a fitting and orderly way.
Now, brothers and sisters, I'm reminding you of the Good News I preached to you, which you received and now stand in.
Through this message you're being saved, if you hold firmly to what I preached to you—unless your faith was for nothing.
What I passed on to you as most important is what I also received: Christ died for our sins, just as the Scriptures said.
He was buried and was raised on the third day, just as the Scriptures said.
He appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
After that, he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at once. Most of them are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, and after that to all the apostles.
Last of all, he appeared to me too, as to someone born at the wrong time.
I'm the least of the apostles and don't deserve to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God's church.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace to me wasn't wasted. I worked harder than all of them—though it wasn't really me, but God's grace working with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
If we preach that Christ was raised from the dead, how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
If the dead aren't raised, then Christ wasn't raised either.
And if Christ wasn't raised, our preaching is pointless, and your faith is pointless too.
Then we'd also be false witnesses about God, because we testified that he raised Christ from the dead—which he couldn't have done if the dead aren't raised.
If the dead aren't raised, Christ wasn't raised either.
And if Christ wasn't raised, your faith is useless and you're still guilty of your sins.
Then those who died trusting Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we're more pitiful than anyone.
But Christ really has been raised from the dead. He is the first of a great harvest of those who have died.
Death came through a human being, and resurrection from the dead also comes through a human being.
Just as everyone dies because of Adam, everyone who belongs to Christ will be made alive.
But each in the right order: Christ first, then, when he comes, those who belong to him.
Then the end will come, when Christ hands the Kingdom over to God the Father, after he has brought every ruler, authority, and power to nothing.
He must reign until he has placed all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
Scripture says, ‘He has placed everything under his feet.’ When it says ‘everything,’ that clearly doesn't include God, who placed everything under Christ.
When everything has been placed under Christ, then the Son himself will also be subject to the one who placed everything under him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what are people doing when they are baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead aren't raised at all, why be baptized on their behalf?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
Brothers and sisters, I face death every day—this is as true as my pride in you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
What did I gain by fighting wild animals in Ephesus—if it was only for human reasons? If the dead aren't raised, then ‘Let's eat and drink, because tomorrow we die.’
Don't be fooled: ‘Bad company ruins good character.’
Come to your senses and stop sinning. Some of you don't know God at all. I say this to your shame.
But someone may ask, ‘How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?’
Don't be foolish. What you plant doesn't come to life unless it first dies.
And what you plant isn't the body that will be. It's only a bare seed, perhaps wheat or something else.
But God gives it a body as he chooses, and each kind of seed gets its own body.
Not all flesh is the same: humans have one kind, animals another, birds another, and fish another.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is different from the glory of the earthly.
The sun has one kind of glory, the moon another, and the stars another. Even one star differs from another in glory.
It's the same with the resurrection of the dead. The body is planted perishable and raised imperishable.
It's planted in dishonor and raised in glory; planted in weakness and raised in power.
It's planted as a natural body and raised as a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
Scripture says, ‘The first man, Adam, became a living being.’ The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual doesn't come first. The natural comes first, and then the spiritual.
The first man came from the earth and was made of dust; the second man came from heaven.
Those made from dust are like the man of dust, and those who belong to heaven are like the man from heaven.
Just as we've borne the image of the man made of dust, we'll also bear the image of the man from heaven.
Brothers and sisters, here's what I mean: flesh and blood can't inherit God's Kingdom, and what decays can't inherit what never decays.
Listen, I'm telling you a mystery: we won't all die, but we will all be changed.
It will happen in a flash, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. The trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
This perishable body must put on what can't decay, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
When this perishable body has put on what can't decay, and this mortal body has put on immortality, then the Scripture will come true: ‘Death has been swallowed up in victory.’
‘Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?’
Death's sting is sin, and sin gets its power from the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm and don't be shaken. Always give yourselves fully to the Lord's work, because you know that your work in the Lord isn't wasted.
Now, about the collection for God's people: do what I directed the churches in Galatia to do.
On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside an amount in keeping with your income, so no collection has to be taken when I arrive.
When I get there, I'll send the people you approve, with letters, to deliver your generous gift to Jerusalem.
If it's appropriate for me to go too, they'll travel with me.
I'll visit you after I go through Macedonia, since I'm traveling through there.
I may stay with you for a while, perhaps even spend the winter, so you can help me on my way wherever I go.
I don't want to see you just briefly. I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord allows.
I'll stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
because a great opportunity for effective work has opened up for me, and there are many who oppose it.
If Timothy comes, make sure he has nothing to fear while he's with you. He's doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
So don't let anyone look down on him. Help him continue his journey in peace so he can come to me. I'm expecting him along with the brothers.
About our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to visit you with the brothers, but he wasn't willing to go just now. He'll come when he gets the chance.
Stay alert! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
Let everything you do be done in love.
You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and that they've devoted themselves to serving God's people. I urge you, brothers and sisters,
to submit to people like them, and to everyone who works and labors alongside them.
I'm glad Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived. They supplied what was missing from your support,
and they refreshed my spirit and yours. Show appreciation for people like them.
The churches in Asia send greetings. Aquila and Priscilla warmly greet you in the Lord, along with the church that meets in their home.
All the brothers and sisters send their greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.
If anyone doesn't love the Lord, let them be cursed. Our Lord, come!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
